title: Qatar Says LNG Damage May Take Years to Repair
summary:
Joining Bloomberg This Weekend, Qatar Central Bank Governor and Qatar Investment Authority Chairman Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani says damage to the country’s LNG facilities could take two to three years to repair, with the conflict contributing to a 7% economic contraction even as the non-hydrocarbon economy grows. He says Qatar’s strong fiscal position has allowed QIA to continue investing globally, with technology and AI among its major areas of focus, while the central bank is deploying AI across its own operations.

At the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: State Street Sees Resilience Driving Portfolios
summary:
State Street Investment Management CEO Yie-Hsin Hung says investors have entered an era where resilient portfolios are increasingly important as higher capital costs, geopolitical tensions and technological change create a wider range of potential outcomes. Hung tells Bloomberg This Weekend hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that institutional investors are adding liquidity and other portfolio buffers, while State Street is also expanding access to private markets and providing the default ETF for the US government's Trump Accounts program.

At the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Rubio Takes on Expansive Foreign Policy Role
summary:
Bloomberg News State Department reporter Eric Martin joins Bloomberg This Weekend and says Secretary of State Marco Rubio has embraced an unusually broad portfolio in the Trump administration, simultaneously serving as national security adviser while taking leading roles on Venezuela, Cuba and other foreign-policy priorities. Martin tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Rubio has largely worked behind the scenes on Iran while adapting his positions to his executive-branch role, a shift examined in Bloomberg Businessweek’s recent profile of the secretary.

At the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Can India Turn Its Promise Into Prosperity?
summary: Blackstone COO Jon Gray says India’s young population, expanding middle class and improving infrastructure are drawing interest from global investors. But India’s demographic advantage also creates pressure: millions of young people graduate every year, while formal-sector job creation has not kept pace with their skills and expectations. At the same time, Indian states are competing aggressively for investment by cutting regulatory barriers, building industrial infrastructure and targeting sectors from electronics to semiconductors. The question is whether India can turn its scale, talent and investment momentum into enough productive jobs to sustain its growth. This version corrects a map of India. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Franklin CEO Says AI Payoff Remains Unclear
summary:
Franklin Templeton CEO Jenny Johnson says companies cannot afford to slow their adoption of AI even as questions persist about costs, governance and the eventual profitability of the technology. Johnson tells hosts of Bloomberg This Weekend David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Franklin has already seen productivity and sales gains from AI, while warning that the economics of increasingly capital-intensive AI companies remain uncertain.

title: Qatar Reshapes Its Wealth Fund Strategy With New Local Platform
summary: Qatar is setting up a dedicated platform to manage and grow its wealth fund’s domestic portfolio worth hundreds of billions of dollars, marking a radical reshaping of the gas-rich country’s sovereign investing landscape.

title: Mnuchin Sees Long-Term Opportunity in Middle East
summary:
Former US Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin says Middle East investment faces short-term uncertainty from the Iran conflict but argues the region remains attractive over the longer term. Mnuchin called for strict enforcement of sanctions on Iran, including potential action against Chinese banks, while saying the US and China should also seek a broader understanding on AI.

title: Jane Street Joins Wave of Dealers Offering Swaps for Risky ETFs
summary: Jane Street Group has begun providing swaps to a swelling cohort of leveraged ETFs, amping up the competition in a niche but lucrative corner of the derivatives market.

title: Qatar Works to Bridge Gap in US Iran Talks
summary:
Qatar’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al-Ansari says mediators are shuttling between capitals and exchanging proposals in an effort to restart negotiations between the US and Iran, with teams working around the clock to bridge remaining differences. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend, Al-Ansari says Qatar’s priorities are ending the conflict and restoring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, warning that restrictions on international waterways could set a dangerous precedent.

At the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Oaktree’s Marks Says He Wants a Less Activist Central Bank
summary: Howard Marks, co-chair of Oaktree Capital Management, said he prefers less communication from the Federal Reserve as Chair Kevin Warsh seeks to works to curtail some guidance that he’s said has hamstrung the central bank in recent years.

title: Marsh CEO Says Geopolitics Tops CEO Risks
summary:
Marsh CEO & President John Doyle says geopolitical tensions and their impact on trade and supply chains are among the biggest concerns facing corporate leaders, while emerging technology is adding to cyber threats. Doyle also tells Bloomberg This Weekend hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that AI offers significant opportunities for growth and productivity but warns that systemic cyber risk stemming from new technologies remains poorly understood.

At the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AI’s Wobbly House of Cards Puts Markets and US Economy at Risk
summary: The heads of America’s leading AI development labs have started a national conversation about tapping the brakes on a technology that’s offering so much promise for society, while at the same time showing it can do a frightening amount of harm.

title: Qatar Airways Bets on Fleet and Cargo Growth
summary: Joining Bloomberg This Weekend, Qatar Airways Group CEO Hamad Ali Al-Khater says passenger demand remains resilient despite regional conflict and sharply higher jet fuel costs, with travelers booking closer to departure and the carrier shifting capacity toward its most profitable routes. The airline plans to take delivery of 138 aircraft over the next five years while expanding its cargo business and continuing its Starlink rollout. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Global Conflicts Shape High Stakes UN Meetings
summary:
World leaders are gathering in New York for the UN General Assembly as escalating Middle East tensions, the war in Ukraine and pressure on global energy supplies dominate the diplomatic agenda. Bloomberg News managing editor for European economy & government Ben Sills and CNN senior national security reporter Jennifer Hansler join Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss Europe’s push for Ukrainian air defenses, the US approach to the Houthis and the prospects for diplomacy as Saudi Arabia faces renewed attacks. 

At the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)
